Homework 7 - Random Walk and Security Simulation

08 Nov 2025

Introduction to Random Walks and Symmetric Binary Processes

While Homework 4 explored the Law of Large Numbers through one-directional accumulation (counting successes from 0 to n), Homework 7 introduces a fundamentally different perspective: the symmetric random walk. Instead of tracking cumulative success rates, we now model a process where each step can move us either up (+1, secure) or down (-1, breached), creating trajectories that can reach both positive and negative scores.

This homework demonstrates how a simple security model—a server facing weekly attacks—naturally leads to one of the most important structures in probability theory and combinatorics: the random walk and its connection to binomial distributions.

Homework 6 - Online Algorithms for Statistical Measures

05 Nov 2025

Introduction to Online Statistical Algorithms

Traditional “batch” algorithms for computing statistical measures like the mean and variance require storing all data points and making multiple passes through the dataset. In contrast, online algorithms (also called streaming algorithms or incremental algorithms) update statistics as each new data point arrives, requiring only constant memory and a single pass through the data.

This homework derives the mathematical foundations for online computation of the arithmetic mean and variance, implements these algorithms, and discusses their advantages from numerical analysis and computational perspectives.

Homework 5 - Measures of Location and Dispersion

05 Nov 2025

Introduction to Statistical Measures

Statistical analysis relies fundamentally on two types of descriptive measures: measures of location (or central tendency) and measures of dispersion (or spread). These measures provide complementary information about data distributions—location measures tell us where the data is centered, while dispersion measures tell us how spread out the data is around that center.

Understanding these measures is essential for data analysis across all scientific disciplines, from experimental physics to social sciences, finance and machine learning.

Homework 4 - Simulating the Law of Large Numbers

28 Oct 2025

Introduction to the Law of Large Numbers

The Law of Large Numbers (LLN) is one of the fundamental theorems in probability theory and statistics. It provides the theoretical foundation for why we can estimate probabilities through repeated experiments and why sample averages converge to expected values.

In this homework, I explore the LLN through simulation and visualization, demonstrating how the relative frequency of successes in repeated Bernoulli trials converges to the true underlying probability as the number of trials increases.
